A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CALIPER research paper, with 21 readable pages including Appendices A–G. Full text and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific content is identical.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix G report original forecasting, runtime, and hyperparameter-sensitivity results on MoCap, TEP, Automobile, and Dysts.

after.justification: Section 3 and Appendix G retain the original forecasting, runtime, and hyperparameter-sensitivity results on all four datasets.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain identical normalization, effective-sample-size gating, weighted local regression, and monotonicity-based retraining procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MoCap, TEP, Automobile, and Dysts datasets and post-drift forecasting scenarios. No training or evaluation coverage changes.

E2.justification: The fixed-window baselines using 128, 512, and 2048 steps and the incremental-update baseline retain identical participation in the corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3 and Appendix F retain the same data splits, learner configurations, detector settings, 30-step input history, prediction horizons of 1/15/30, and MSE/MAE metrics.

E4.justification: The locality-parameter and ESS-threshold sensitivity study in Appendix G and Figure 6 is unchanged, as are the runtime analyses. No analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same statement about multiple independent runs with random seeds shared across algorithms within each run. No run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–6 retain identical numerical entries and plotted results. The reported rankings, trends, and qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, dynamical assumptions, Proposition 1, generalization-bound interpretation, and Appendix E proof are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about data-only retraining readiness, state dependence, predictive performance, and computational overhead.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Appendix C limitations are unchanged, including qualifications concerning non-Markovian dynamics, high-dimensional neighborhoods, and the absence of a universal optimal retraining window.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains identical hyperparameters, hardware, implementation details, and code/data access information. The automobile-data access and redistribution restrictions are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4, Appendix B, and the bibliography are identical. The publication-status header does not revise the paper's relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' on every page and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body wording, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The running publication header and first-page marginal stamp change. Figures, tables, captions, equations, and body layout remain visually identical, with no reflow or relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 only updates publication and version identification. The scientific evidence, explanations, limitations, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality change.
